title: Manicotti
author: Marco Bellini
desc: Manicotti are wide pasta tubes filled with a creamy, herbed ricotta filling, baked in tomato sauce until tender and golden — a comforting vegetarian relative of cannelloni.
longDesc: Where cannelloni is often filled with meat, manicotti's name meaning 'little sleeves' typically refers to a purely cheese-based filling — a simple, satisfying dish popular for family Sunday dinners.
ingredients: 12–14 manicotti tubes (or crepes, as an alternative wrapper)
600 g (21 oz) tomato passata or marinara sauce
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the manicotti tubes just until pliable, slightly under package directions (they will finish cooking in the oven). Drain and lay flat to cool.
In a bowl, combine the ricotta, half the mozzarella, half the Parmigiano, the egg, parsley, oregano, salt, and pepper, mixing until smooth.
Preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Spread a thin layer of tomato sauce on the base of a baking dish.
Fill a piping bag with the ricotta mixture and pipe into each cooked manicotti tube.
Arrange the filled tubes in the baking dish and pour the remaining sauce over the top.
Scatter with the remaining mozzarella and Parmigiano.
Cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes, then uncover and bake a further 10–15 minutes until bubbling and golden.
chefTips: Undercook the pasta tubes slightly before filling — they finish cooking in the oven and can become too soft if fully cooked beforehand.
A piping bag makes filling the delicate tubes far easier and cleaner than a spoon.
Fresh herbs make a noticeable difference in the filling compared to dried alone.
commonMistakes: Fully cooking the pasta before baking, resulting in overly soft, fragile tubes.
Overfilling the tubes, causing them to split.
Using low-moisture pre-shredded mozzarella straight from a bag with anti-caking agents, which can affect melt quality — freshly shredded is best.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 3 days, or freeze baked or unbaked for up to 2 months.
reheating: Reheat covered in a 180°C (350°F) oven for 20 minutes until warmed through.
healthBenefits: A good source of calcium and protein from the cheeses.
culturalNote: Manicotti is more commonly associated with Italian-American home cooking than with a single specific region of Italy, evolving from various stuffed-pasta traditions brought by Southern Italian immigrants.
